init._comment: FLUX mono listening pair, DRY half (spec 2026-07-29-flux-mono section 6). Judges what collapsing FLUX to one BBD line costs in echo width, with the reverb removed so it cannot recover that width and hide the answer. Its twin flux_mono_verb.json is identical but for the two reverb lines below. A wide chord with several voices is deliberate: per-voice pan drift (voice.cpp) is what puts width into the echo's input, and without it a mono-summed echo would be indistinguishable by construction. 24 s gives the 0.05-0.2 Hz drift at least one full cycle.

THE TWO LINES THAT DIFFER BETWEEN THE PAIR. Slot 3 is FXT_REV_SEND (part_fx.h). Killed twice on purpose: set_reverb_mix mutes the return, slot 3 stops the send that feeds it, and stating both makes the intent unmistakable to whoever reads this next.

events._comment: A long tail at high feedback, so the echo has time to separate from the dry signal and its position becomes obvious.

DRIVE sweep. Not about width: with one line the saturator sees the mono SUM, so it bites earlier than it did with two (spec section 4). This makes that change audible in the same file rather than needing its own render.
